headline: Clinton order gives the World Trade Organization legal standing and certain legal protections in the United States, as the WTO agreement requires.
what_it_does: This order carries out, for the United States, Article VIII of the agreement that created the World Trade Organization (WTO). That article says the WTO should have legal capacity, such as the ability to sign contracts and own property, plus certain privileges and immunities. The order puts those terms into effect in the US. No summary was provided, so the exact protections granted are not described here.

who_it_affects.how: It gains legal standing and certain legal protections when it operates in the United States.

who_it_affects.group: WTO officials and staff, and representatives of WTO member countries
who_it_affects.how: They may receive certain privileges and immunities under US law tied to their WTO work.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed April 9, 1997; the start date is not stated in the material provided.
